messages.subject: Independent Events in R
messages.body_plain:
Hi everyone,

I hope you are all doing well. Please forgive me for posting a slightly unrelated question in this group... I am not sure who else to ask..

I have a camera trap data set and wish to extract only the independent events for a given species (a event is considered independent if it is of the same species, at the same camera station, within a given time period e.g., 30 minutes). I can't get my code right. Does anyone on here perhaps have some R code they can share to work out 30 minute independent events?

Thank you in advance,

Best Wishes,
Nia

Hi everyone,

First, I apologize if this is a silly question-- I'm no statistician by any means.

I've built single season, single species occupancy models for red-winged blackbirds during their breeding season following the eBird best practices methods (https://cornelllabofornithology.github.io/ebird-best-practices/occupancy.html). These methods use land cover types as occupancy and detection covariates. messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

I've got a bit of a problem I'm trying to wrap my head around.
I have 109 sites with 19 occasions, studying invasive predators with a site being comprised of a camera facing into a road and another into the bush.

My top model for detection was as follows
m_det<-occuRN(~Road+Effort ~ 1,species).
I then use;
p_det<-predict(m_det,type='det')

to predict which generates 1,620 values.

Road and effort are both observation level covariates i.e. it could be different in each of the 19 occasions. Where Road is whether the road camera was active or not during the occasion (1 or 0).  Effort is the total number of camera-trap nights accrued by both cameras at a site per occasion.

Given this produces a very large matrix with lots of different values, does anyone have any suggestions on how I could go about plotting this relationship to visualise it. I would understand how to do it if these were site level co-variates, but the fact they change with occasion is what is tripping me up.

Thanks,
Tom

messages.body_plain:
For a summary of the detection model you have the number of visits, numbers of varying trap nights, and whether or not the road camera is active or inactive.  So I think you just need to decide on what would be a good summary.

Below I've written some code to generate some data that hopefully mimics your model followed by two possible ways to summarize the detection model.  (Note that I've rebelled against using "<-" for assignment.)

# Generate some data
nSites = 109
nVisits = 19
prOccupancy = 0.6
trapNightsMean = 5

road = matrix(rep(NA, nSites*nVisits), nrow=nSites)
effort = road
y = road
for (site in 1:nSites) {
    status = rbinom(1, 1, prOccupancy)
    for (visit in 1:nVisits) {
        road[site, visit] = rbinom(1, 1, 0.7)
        effort[site, visit] = (1 + rpois(1, trapNightsMean))*(1 + road[site, visit])

        if (status == 1) {
           logit = -3 + 1.2*road[site, visit] + 0.2*effort[site, visit]
           pr = 1 - 1/(1+exp(logit))
           y[site, visit] =  rbinom(1, 1, pr)
        } else {
           road[site, visit] = 0
           y[site, visit] = 0
        }
    }
}

obsCovs <- list(road=road, effort=effort)
library(unmarked)
umf <- unmarkedFrameOccu(y = y, obsCovs = obsCovs)

results = occu(~road + effort ~1, umf)

Now here are two possible ways to summarize the detection model.

# Single visit detection probabilities with varying trap nights with
# road camera active and inactive.
trapNights = (1:10)
# Road camera active
logit1 = with(results@opt, par[2] + par[3] + par[4]*trapNights)
# Road camera inactive
logit0 = with(results@opt, par[2] +          par[4]*trapNights)
par(mai=c(1,1.5,0.5,0.5))
plot(trapNights, 1 - 1/(1+exp(logit1)), las=1, xlab="Trap nights",
  ylab="Probability of detection\nwith a single visit", pch=16,
  ylim=c(0,0.6), cex.lab=1.5, font.lab=2)
points(trapNights, 1 - 1/(1+exp(logit0)))
legend(1, 0.6, c("Inactive", "Active"), pch=c(1,16), title="Road camera")

# Detection probability with 3 trap nights per camera per visit and 19 visits with
# Vary the number of visits with road camera active.
logit1 = with(results@opt, par[2] + par[3] + par[4]*2*3)
logit0 = with(results@opt, par[2] + par[4]*3)
p1 = 1 - 1/(1+exp(logit1))
p0 = 1 - 1/(1+exp(logit0))
nRoadCameraActive = c(0:19)
p = 1 - (1-p1)^nRoadCameraActive * (1-p0)^(19-nRoadCameraActive)
plot(nRoadCameraActive, p, xlab="Number of visits with road camera active",
  ylab="Probability of at least one\ndetection in 19 visits",
  las=1, cex.lab=1.5, font.lab=2, cex.main=2, main="19 total visits", pch=16)
axis(1, c(1:19), rep("", 19), tcl=-0.25)

Confidence intervals can be added but that should wait until you decide what kinds of summaries you want.

Jim

messages.body_plain:
Hi All,

I have more of a philosophical question about occupancy covariates in a 2-species occupancy model fit with occuMulti (apologies if this is not an appropriate question for the group!). I am primarily interested in effects of species A on species B (not vice versa).

My question: Does it make sense to model consider density of species A as a covariate on co-occurrence of species A and B? In this scenario, species A is a group-living species (groups ranging 2-16 individuals) but there also are lone individuals that are not part of a group. I have reason to believe that the effect of species A on species B is better captured by the density of species A in the vicinity (e.g., 200 m) of cameras, not just the presence/absence of species A. But of course, the probability that species A is detected at a given camera is linked to the density of species A in the vicinity of that camera. I've read at least a few publications that modeled detection probability of one species as a function of presence/absence of another species. On the other hand, I have not found any examples that modeled co-occurrence of species A and species B as a function of the density of species A, so I'm not sure if this would be a valid approach. Any guidance would be greatly appreciated!

Thank you in advance!
James
